name: 四季のご馳走家 味彩 (Shiki no Gochisouya Ajisai)

claims.text: Menu includes fried oysters and tempura, which in an izakaya kitchen share fryer oil with wheat-breaded items; no dedicated gluten-free fryer is mentioned.
Sashimi and shellfish are served with standard soy sauce, and a signature wakame dish uses bonito-dashi ponzu (soy-based) — typical Japanese shoyu/ponzu is brewed with wheat.
Bonito (katsuo) dashi is explicitly used (e.g. wakame with bonito-dashi ponzu); fish stock is likely present in many dishes that otherwise appear vegetable-based.
Very fresh raw fish and shellfish straight from the tank and local port means plain sashimi can be eaten without sauce if the diner brings or requests a wheat-free alternative.
As a traditional sushi counter, soy sauce is integral to the meal and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat; no wheat-free alternative is mentioned.
The shop is centered entirely on Ise Bay fish and shellfish with sake accompaniments; no plant-based or vegan items are offered.

name: 天びん屋 本店 (Tenbinya Honten)

claims.text: Menu includes wheat-breaded fried shrimp (ebi fry) and tempura, indicating shared fryer oil with no documented dedicated gluten-free fryer.
Seafood bowls, sashimi, and tekone sushi are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which typically contains wheat; no wheat-free tamari is advertised.
Regional Ise udon is a wheat noodle served in a dark soy-based sauce.
Kitchen is centered on fish and shellfish, and rice/noodle dishes such as kamameshi and Ise udon are typically prepared with katsuo (bonito)/kombu dashi; no plant-based menu is published.
Sashimi (e.g., Ise-lobster) is served with two kinds of soy sauce; standard soy sauce contains wheat.
A dedicated shellfish-grill house; a clam-dashi (seafood broth) butter rice is offered, and the menu centers on oysters, lobster and other shellfish.
Shellfish is grilled to order in its own shell after being chosen live from the tank, so plainly grilled or salt-seasoned shellfish can be requested without added sauces.

name: 鳥羽国際ホテル 和食レストラン もんど岬 (Toba Kokusai Hotel Washoku Restaurant Mondo )

claims.text: The hotel states it cannot accept dietary requests where trace amounts or cross-contamination (コンタミネーション) could trigger severe symptoms, nor cases involving multiple allergens — meaning strict celiac-level avoidance cannot be guaranteed.
As a kaiseki-style washoku restaurant, dishes rely on soy sauce and wheat-containing seasonings; no wheat-free shoyu is advertised.

Seafood-centered kitchen using bonito/kombu dashi as standard; plant-based meals would be a special off-menu arrangement, so cross-contact with fish-derived stock is a real risk unless explicitly arranged.

The hotel runs a formal food-allergy intake: download the allergy inquiry sheet (食物アレルギーお伺いシート) and submit by fax or email at least 4 days before the reservation; listed allergens include wheat, egg, dairy, soba, peanut, and soy.
Vegetarian/vegan accommodation is listed as available with advance arrangement.
A structured advance allergy-sheet process exists, so needs can be communicated in writing before arrival.
提供形態が産直市場併設の食堂／ビュッフェ系で、天ぷら・かき揚げ・フライなど小麦衣の揚げ物が共有の場・共有油で多数提供される。共有トングや配膳での交差汚染リスクが高い。
専用フライヤーやグルテンフリー対応に関する記載はどの公式ページにも見当たらない。
てこね寿司（醤油漬けの地魚を使う郷土料理）や煮物など、小麦を含む通常の醤油を使う料理が並ぶ。
お野菜の煮もの・カレー・グラタン・郷土料理にはだし（鰹節）・魚介・乳・醤油など動物性が含まれる可能性が高く、海産物中心の施設のため共有配膳での魚介の混入も想定される。
よくある質問・公式各ページにアレルギー、グルテン、ベジタリアン／ヴィーガン対応の記載はなく、対応可否は確認できない。個別対応はメール／電話での事前問い合わせが必要（info@tobamarche.jp / 0599-21-1080）。
サラダ、お野菜の煮もの、刺身、天婦羅、フライ、グラタン、カレーなど25種類以上の地産地消料理が並び、野菜料理の品数はあるため菜食寄りの選択は一定可能。
地元の農産物・水産物の産直市場が併設され、生鮮野菜や果物をその場で購入できる。

name: 鳥羽の食堂 海誠 (Toba no Shokudo Kaisei)

claims.text: Menu features wheat-breaded fried items (large shrimp fry, tonkatsu, miso katsu) typically cooked in a shared fryer; high cross-contamination risk and no dedicated fryer indicated.
Sashimi and seafood bowls are served with soy sauce, which is conventionally brewed with wheat; no gluten-free tamari is mentioned.
Entirely seafood- and meat-based menu; dashi and seasonings on rice and sides are likely bonito/katsuo-based, making hidden fish stock a concern for anything ordered.
Open all-you-can-eat buffet with a stone-oven pizza station, fried/breaded items, and a shared serving line, making cross-contact with wheat very likely; no dedicated fryer indicated.
The kitchen states that allergens contained in condiments and broths (e.g., soy sauce, dashi) may not be reflected on the per-dish allergen labels.
Seafood-forward buffet; fish, bonito/katsuo dashi, and animal products are pervasive and shared serving utensils are used across dishes.
Individual buffet dishes are marked with colored allergen seals covering eggs, crustaceans, wheat, dairy, and sesame/nuts; guests with allergies not shown are asked to consult staff.
The inn lists 'allergy display available' (アレルギー表示あり) among its dining services.
Per-dish allergen labeling is provided at the buffet for major allergens including wheat, which lets diners screen many items at a glance.
A salad bar, fresh vegetables, fruit, and freshly cooked local rice give some naturally lower-risk options.
